  "text": "On the morning the bakery closed, Lena found a small brass key beneath the till. A paper label hung from it, blank except for a grease stain.

Her father was outside, scraping his name from the window.

“What does this open?” she asked.

He glanced through the glass and shrugged.

She tried the cupboard under the stairs, then the drawer where they kept birthday candles. Neither lock accepted it.

By ten, the last customers had collected their orders. Mrs. Vale took six rolls and asked whether they would freeze. A man Lena had never seen bought the remaining biscuits without asking the price.

Her father came inside carrying the scraper.

“There’s still the upstairs room,” he said.

They had used it for flour sacks until the ceiling began to leak. Behind the empty shelving stood a wooden box Lena remembered sitting on as a child.

The key turned reluctantly.

Inside were notebooks, each wrapped in a flour bag. She opened one to a page headed Tuesday. Beneath it, in her mother’s handwriting, were three names and three sums.

“People who owed us?” Lena asked.

Her father shook his head.

“People who couldn’t.”

Page after page: names, loaves, occasional cakes. Some entries had been crossed out. Beside one, her mother had drawn a small star.

“What’s that mean?”

“I don’t remember.”

Lena closed the notebook. Downstairs, the bell rang above the door, although she had turned the sign around.

Her father listened.

“Would you see who that is?” he asked.

She left the box open and went down. He followed more slowly, carrying the six rolls Mrs. Vale had forgotten."
